notes:
Executive summary: mid-market B2B product company evaluating Redwood Hosted API for quick rollout of an in-app chat + knowledge search, with Dedicated considered for steady-state cost predictability and throughput.

Discovery / requirements (from AE/SE calls):
- Primary workload: real-time chat support (multi-tenant), supplement with vector search/embeddings for docs.
- Latency target: median <= 300ms token generation for short replies (~25-80 tokens), p95 < 700ms.
- Throughput target: steady 30-45 RPS during business hours, burst to 120 RPS during peak events.
- Cost sensitivity: high. CFO signaled need to cut per-token spend by ~40% vs prototype with direct cloud-hosted LLMs.
- Models: prefer open models (Llama-2/3 family or Falcon-like) but ok with verified proprietary variants if unit economics better.
- Routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to lower-cost model for non-critical queries; can tolerate slightly lower quality for non-priority routes.
- Security: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML for admin users, audit logs for token-level usage, EU data residency for EU customers.

Engagement timeline (highlights):
- 2026-02-20: Intro call (AE: Maya) - qual, use-case mapping, sent quickstart.
- 2026-02-25: Demo of Hosted API (SE: Diego) - streaming + function-calling walkthrough.
- 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-09: 2-week Hosted API POC (sandbox) - integrated chat widget, metrics collection.
- 2026-03-05: Cost workshop (workshop #1) - Redwood team presented batching/caching levers; ran unit-econ exercises.
- 2026-03-08: Deep-dive quantization session (SE-led) - discussed q4/int8 profiles, expected perf and accuracy impact on their prompts.
- 2026-03-10: Onsite pricing review (virtual) - AE + Finance + Product leads; requested Dedicated pricing options and SLA details.

POC outcomes & observations:
- Baseline (POC) used hosted medium Llama-variant, naive per-request handling -> estimated $X per 1M tokens.
- With batching suggestion (continuous batching 16-32 tokens window) + prefix (KV) caching on doc vectors, Redwood's proposed config reduces token ops by 28-40% in workload sim.
- Quantization options: q4_0 for throughput-focused routes (approx +2-3x throughput, ~30-45% token cost reduction), int8 experimentation for service critical routes where latency dominates. SE noted jitter trade-offs on small seq lengths.
- Routing policy recommended: hot-path chat on Dedicated low-latency nodes, background reranking and non-sensitive embed jobs routed to lower-cost pools / hosted variants.
- Expected overall unit-economics improvement: 35-55% cost reduction vs baseline depending on chosen quant profile and batching aggressiveness.

Commercial / procurement notes:
- Interested in 12-month Dedicated commit if Redwood can guarantee ingress latency SLOs and provide a migration credit for first 3 months.
- Requesting line-item pricing for: Dedicated capacity (GPU types), burst capacity, 24/7 premium support, extra observability retention (90d).
- Legal asked for specific data residency clause for EU customers and KMS integration details. SE provided security FAQ link (drive).

Open technical questions (to resolve in next week):
- Confirm Dedicated GPU SKU options and expected cold-starts for KV cache when scaling replicas.
- More granular simulation of their token distribution (short chat vs long context) to finalize optimal batching window.
- Full quantization regression checklist on their prompt set (SE to run with Redwood Optimize).

Next actions (short):
- Redwood: deliver Dedicated price sheet + example commitment structures by 2026-03-14 (Maya).
- SE (Diego): run quantization regression on 150 sample prompts and share trade-off matrix by 2026-03-16.
- SparrowField: schedule procurement + legal review; aim to sign LOI before end-April if pricing acceptable.

Notes style: shorthand, snippets from calls, some direct quotes: "If we can get 40% off token costs without dropping chat quality we're happy to move to committed Dedicated" — Head of Product.
